rater: Assistant; non-blind review of the user's posted captions against all five saved reference captions, sound labels and clip-duration metadata. No waveform listening.
rules: Review the main asserted sound-source/event claims in each caption; normalize ordinary paraphrases and deduplicate repetitions. A claim can bundle a source with its activity; this is not exhaustive atomic-proposition annotation.
Supported means at least one reference or label provides semantic support, allowing a coarser description of a source/event. It does not mean verified against the waveform.

Unreferenced means an asserted specific sound/source lacks support in the supplied annotations. It does not mean verified absent. Specific identity can be unsupported even if the general sound is supported.
Unclear means malformed text, insufficient action/material detail or conflicting annotations prevent a confident reference judgment.

Source-mismatch candidates identify a competing concrete source assignment for an event whose source the annotations describe differently. Candidate membership does not establish acoustic absence or exclusivity.

Exclude generic background-noise mentions, abstract nouns, moods and explanations of typical source behavior from the main sound-claim count. Record hypothetical sources/settings separately; do not treat lists of examples as assertions that every example is present.

Do not systematically score timing/order, pitch, intensity, counts or negation. Record salient reference contradictions and metadata errors separately. Preserve this limited scope when interpreting aggregate scores.
The headline statistic is caption-level annotation support, not claim precision or a CHAIR/ECHO reproduction. Informal claim grouping makes pooled claim percentages inappropriate.
Reference omissions are qualitative audit notes, not an exhaustive coverage metric. All-main-claims-supported does not mean complete, fluent, temporally correct or hallucination-free.
This is an exploratory audit performed after inspecting results and prompt weaknesses, not a blind or held-out evaluation. No audio judge or additional trained model is used.
